knowledge_delta.summary: NIST AI RMF opens a new AI-governance branch: a cross-cutting governance function plus context mapping, risk measurement and explicit risk response. No prior graph concept is close enough to reuse without collapsing implementation controls into the framework itself.

items.label: AI RMF Core
items.source_basis: AI RMF 1.0 organizes practical AI risk management around GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE outcomes and explicitly says the actions are not a checklist or mandatory ordered steps.
items.prior_basis: The project has architecture, policy, observability and decision concepts but no use-case-agnostic AI risk-management operating framework.
items.interpretation: The Core becomes a reusable layer for structuring AI risk decisions without pretending that one control implementation equals the framework.

items.label: Cross-cutting AI governance
items.source_basis: GOVERN is designed to inform and be infused throughout MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE rather than ending after an initial setup phase.
items.prior_basis: Existing governance-related concepts describe specific execution or policy mechanisms, not organizational accountability and risk culture across an AI lifecycle.
items.interpretation: Governance is modeled as persistent organizational capability and decision ownership rather than a one-time compliance gate.

items.label: AI risk context mapping
items.source_basis: MAP recognizes context, purpose, affected actors and context-related risks before those risks are measured or managed.
items.prior_basis: No prior concept explicitly models AI risk as dependent on deployment context and affected actors.
items.interpretation: Context becomes a prerequisite for selecting evidence and controls instead of treating generic model metrics as universally meaningful.

items.label: AI risk measurement and monitoring
items.source_basis: MEASURE applies quantitative, qualitative or mixed methods to assess, benchmark and monitor mapped AI risks and trustworthiness-related impacts.
items.prior_basis: Existing project evaluation/observability concepts do not provide a general AI risk-assessment function tied to context and risk-management decisions.
items.interpretation: Measurement is treated as evidence for risk decisions, not as telemetry volume or model benchmarking for its own sake.

items.label: AI risk prioritization and response
items.source_basis: MANAGE prioritizes assessed risks, develops responses and includes explicit determinations about whether development or deployment should proceed.
items.prior_basis: No prior concept provides a general lifecycle risk-response function that converts assessment results into proceed/mitigate/monitor/stop decisions.
items.interpretation: The framework's value culminates in visible risk decisions and treatment, not merely in documenting risks or measurements.

claims.text: AI RMF 1.0 is intended as a voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific and use-case-agnostic resource for organizations managing AI risks.
The AI RMF Core is organized around GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE, with GOVERN cross-cutting; the functions and actions are not a mandatory checklist or rigid ordered workflow.

evidence.locator: AIRC AI RMF Core → functions are not checklist/ordered steps

claims.text: GOVERN establishes organizational structures, policies, roles, culture and accountability and remains a continual cross-cutting requirement throughout AI risk management.
The MAP function builds contextual knowledge about the AI system and identifies risks related to its purpose, setting, affected actors and potential impacts.
The MEASURE function uses qualitative, quantitative or mixed methods to assess, benchmark and monitor mapped AI risks and trustworthiness-related impacts.
The MANAGE function prioritizes assessed AI risks, develops responses and includes explicit determinations about whether a system's development or deployment should proceed.

AI RMF outcomes should not be mistaken for a universal technical-controls checklist; the Playbook provides optional suggested actions that organizations tailor to context and are not expected to implement in full.

evidence.locator: AIRC AI RMF Core → categories/subcategories are outcomes/actions, not checklist
NIST AI RMF Playbook FAQs → not expected to implement all suggestions / not ordered steps

claims.note: The distinction between framework outcomes and implementation controls is the project's synthesis of NIST's explicit non-checklist and tailoring guidance.

prerequisite_map.summary: The framework is coherent once the reader understands the Core as an operating layer, GOVERN as cross-cutting capability, MAP as context, MEASURE as evidence and MANAGE as the decision/response function.

items.label: AI RMF Core
items.reason: The reader needs the Core as a single operating model before categories and Playbook suggestions can be interpreted without turning them into checklist fragments.

items.label: Cross-cutting AI governance
items.reason: The model is misread if governance is treated as a first phase that ends rather than an organizational capability active throughout risk work.

items.label: AI risk context mapping
items.reason: Measurements and controls cannot be selected intelligently until the system purpose, actors, impacts and context-specific risks are explicit.

items.label: AI risk measurement and monitoring
items.reason: AI risk management needs evidence about mapped risks rather than only principles, policies or generic model metrics.

items.label: AI risk prioritization and response
items.reason: Evidence only becomes risk management when it is prioritized and converted into treatment, resource and lifecycle decisions.

learning_prompt.retention_prompt: Without looking back, reconstruct NIST AI RMF 1.0 as an operating model rather than a checklist: explain what GOVERN contributes continuously, what MAP must establish before testing, what MEASURE adds, what MANAGE decides, and why the framework still needs context-specific controls and evidence.

transfer_prompt.prompt: A team wants to deploy an AI agent that can approve refunds. Before choosing a specific policy engine or evaluation metric, use the AI RMF operating model to state what must be governed, what deployment context and affected actors must be mapped, what evidence should be measured, and which risk decision the organization must explicitly make.

source_decision.rationale: The explainer preserves the four-function operating model and its non-checklist boundary, but the original framework is still worth skimming where exact categories, governance responsibilities and MANAGE decisions matter because those details determine how a real organization tailors the framework without inventing its own meaning.

novelty.reason: This source opens a new AI risk-management and governance branch rather than repeating existing agent, policy or observability architecture concepts.

source_quality.reason: The primary source is the official NIST AI RMF 1.0 publication, with official AIRC and Playbook material used to verify the operating boundaries.

relevance.reason: The framework provides a practical structure for enterprise AI decisions, especially when teams need to connect governance, context, testing evidence and deployment choices.

practical_leverage.reason: The model can immediately structure AI risk workshops, evidence plans, ownership and proceed/stop decisions without requiring a new technical platform.

compression_loss.reason: The central model compresses well, but exact categories/subcategories and trustworthiness guidance are intentionally omitted and matter when operationalizing the framework in a real program.
